identificationModule.briefTitle: Evaluating the Dietary Supplement Anatabloc in Thyroid Health-ASAP (Antabloc Supplementation Autoimmune Prevention)
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Potential Effects of the Dietary Supplement Anatabloc on Antithyroid Autoantibodies and Thyroid Function in Autoimmune Thyroiditis

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and potential effects of Anatabloc dietary supplementation on antithyroid autoantibodies, thyroid structure, and thyroid function in subjects with autoimmune thyroiditis.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a 5-visit, 12-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study.

armGroups.label: Placebo
armGroups.description: subject takes one oral placebo lozenge, three times per day

armGroups.label: Anatabloc Supplement
armGroups.description: subject takes one oral Supplement lozenge, three time per day

interventions.name: Anatabloc Supplement
interventions.description: Product, as mint-flavored lozenges (3 mg anatabine per lozenge), to be taken 3 times each day

interventions.name: Placebo
interventions.description: Placebo, as mint flavored lozenges, to be taken 3 times each day

primaryOutcomes.measure: Numbers of subjects experiencing adverse effects as a measure of safety
primaryOutcomes.description: Collected data on the numbers and types of any adverse effects related to the use of Anatabloc by subjects

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Measured changes in markers of autoimmune thyroiditis: changes in blood levels of anti-thyroid auto-antibodies, and changes in the volume and vascularization of the thyroid
secondaryOutcomes.description: To determine if dietary supplementation with Anatabloc has an effect on antithyroid autoantibody levels, thyroid structure, and/or thyroid function in subjects with autoimmune thyroiditis

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* adults 18-70 years of age
* having positive antibodies against thyroid peroxidase
* having sonographic evidence consistent with a diagnosis of Hashimoto's thyroiditis

Exclusion Criteria:

* having evidence of end-stage thyroiditis
* being a current smoker or smokeless tobacco user
* be taking systemic glucocorticoids, interferon-alpha, anti-CD20 antibody, or anti-CTLA-4 antibody
* be taking any medication for treatment of autoimmune thyroiditis other than L-thyroxine or equivalent

references.citation: Schmeltz LR, Blevins TC, Aronoff SL, Ozer K, Leffert JD, Goldberg MA, Horowitz BS, Bertenshaw RH, Troya P, Cohen AE, Lanier RK, Wright C 4th. Anatabine supplementation decreases thyroglobulin antibodies in patients with chronic lymphocytic autoimmune (Hashimoto's) thyroiditis: a randomized controlled clinical trial. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2014 Jan;99(1):E137-42. doi: 10.1210/jc.2013-2951. Epub 2013 Dec 20.
